lessons.title: Basis of Ideology and Democracy in Islam
lessons.notes_html:
What Is an Ideology?

An ideology includes organised ideas about life and thought. Together these shape people's thinking, character and social life.

  • Beliefs
  • Views
  • Aims of life
  • Customs and traditions
  • Culture
  • Way of life

Sources of the Islamic Ideology

The sources of an ideology are its basic origins. The Islamic ideology has three sources:

No.SourceExplanation
1The Holy QuranThe first and basic origin of the Islamic ideology
2The Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH)The second basic origin of the Islamic ideology
3Customs and traditionsCustoms and traditions in the light of Islamic teachings

Importance of an Ideology

An ideology is very important for a nation, because without it no nation can progress.

  • It mirrors the thoughts and thinking of the people.
  • It unites them on one platform.
  • It guides national movements.
  • It helps in choosing leaders.
  • It prepares people to sacrifice for their cause.

Principles of Democracy in Islam

  • Justice: Putting everything in its right place.
  • Equality: No distinction on the basis of colour, race, language, belief or wealth; all people are equal before the law.
  • Brotherhood: All Muslims are brothers to one another.
  • Tolerance: Respect for and forbearance towards the views and beliefs of others.

Place of National Character in an Ideology

National character is formed in the light of an ideology. When people have firm faith in their ideology, such character makes a nation strong.

  • They dedicate their lives and property to it.
  • They work with honesty and integrity.
  • They love their homeland and work hard.
  • They prefer the national interest over personal interest.

Key Points

  • Arranging things in their proper place is called justice. The literal meaning of justice is to put everything in its right place.
  • Faith rests on the Oneness of Allah (Tawhid) and the Prophethood (Risalat). The most important aspects of a Muslim's faith are complete belief in the Oneness of Allah and in the Prophethood of the last Prophet (PBUH).
  • Ukhuwwat means brotherhood. The Holy Quran says that all believers are brothers to one another.
  • The sources of the Islamic ideology are the Holy Quran and the Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH).

mcqs.q: What does an ideology consist of?
options: Only a set of religious rituals
Organised ideas about life and thought
Only the economic rules of a country
Only the political laws of a state
mcqs.why: The correct answer is organised ideas about life and thought. An ideology includes such organised ideas, and together they shape people's thinking, character and social life, which is why it is more than rituals or laws alone.

mcqs.q: Which is the first and basic source (origin) of the Islamic ideology?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Holy Quran. The lesson lists three sources of the Islamic ideology and clearly calls the Holy Quran its first and basic origin, with the Sunnah as the second basic origin.

mcqs.q: Which is the second basic source of the Islamic ideology?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Sunnah of the Prophet (PBUH). After the Holy Quran, the Sunnah is the second basic origin of the Islamic ideology, while customs and traditions count only when seen in the light of Islamic teachings.

mcqs.q: In the principles of democracy in Islam, what does justice mean?
options: Giving everyone equal wealth by force
Obeying the ruler in every matter
Putting everything in its right place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is putting everything in its right place. The lesson explains the literal meaning of justice in exactly these words, and it is one of the principles of democracy in Islam along with equality, brotherhood and tolerance.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, equality in Islam means that:
options: Only the rich and the poor are equal
There is no distinction on the basis of colour, race, language, belief or wealth, and all people are equal before the law
Only people of one language are equal
Equality applies only in religious matters
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that there is no distinction on the basis of colour, race, language, belief or wealth. Islam treats all people as equal before the law, so this equality is complete and is not limited to one group or one field.

mcqs.q: What does the Arabic word 'Ukhuwwat' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brotherhood. The lesson states that Ukhuwwat means brotherhood and quotes the Holy Quran that all believers are brothers to one another, which is a basic principle of the Islamic social order.

mcqs.q: Which principle of democracy in Islam means respect for and forbearance towards the views and beliefs of others?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is tolerance. The lesson defines tolerance as respect for and forbearance towards the views and beliefs of others, while justice, equality and brotherhood each have their own separate meanings.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, what happens to a nation that has no ideology?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it cannot progress. The lesson stresses that an ideology is very important for a nation because without it no nation can progress; it unites the people on one platform and guides their movements.

mcqs.q: One importance of an ideology is that it:
options: Prepares people to sacrifice for their cause
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it prepares people to sacrifice for their cause. The lesson lists this among the importance of an ideology, together with uniting people on one platform, guiding national movements and helping in choosing leaders.

mcqs.q: People who have firm faith in their ideology show national character by:
options: Preferring personal interest over the nation
Preferring the national interest over personal interest
Avoiding hard work for the homeland
mcqs.why: The correct answer is preferring the national interest over personal interest. The lesson says firm faith in the ideology builds national character: such people work with honesty and integrity, love their homeland and put the nation before themselves.

lessons.title: Ideology of Pakistan — Quaid-e-Azam and Allama Iqbal
lessons.notes_html:
Basis of the Ideology of Pakistan

The ideology of Pakistan is based on Islam (the Islamic ideology). The ideology of Pakistan rests on the basic beliefs and teachings of Islam. Islam is the most truly democratic, because in Islam all people are equal before the law and the ruler is the representative of the people.

Sayings of the Quaid-e-Azam

The Quaid-e-Azam (1876-1948) said that Pakistan does not merely mean obtaining a piece of land; we want to build a laboratory where we can enforce our practical system on Islamic principles.

  • At the Muslim League session in Lahore on 23 March 1940 he clarified the ideological basis of the Islamic state.
  • In January 1941 he said that India has never been one country or one nation.
  • He said that Hinduism and Islam are two separate social and civil systems, so the two nations cannot be merged into one nation.

Statement of Allama Iqbal

Allama Iqbal (1877-1938) gave his statement about the ideology of Pakistan in his presidential address at the annual session of the All India Muslim League at Allahabad in December 1930.

  • He said that India is not one country but a small subcontinent, inhabited by people of different religions and languages.
  • He said that the Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan should be combined into a separate state for the Muslims.
  • This separate state would be the final destination of the Muslims of north-west India.

Key Points

  • The ideology of Pakistan is based on Islam.
  • Islam is the most truly democratic.
  • Allama Iqbal gave his statement about the ideology of Pakistan in his presidential address at Allahabad in 1930.
  • The Quaid-e-Azam said that Hinduism and Islam are different social systems.
  • Character, habits and manners are the reflection of an ideology.

mcqs.q: On what is the ideology of Pakistan based?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Islam. The lesson states clearly that the ideology of Pakistan is based on Islam and rests on the basic beliefs and teachings of Islam, not on any imported political system.

mcqs.q: Why is Islam described as the most truly democratic?
options: Because it has the largest population
Because in Islam all people are equal before the law and the ruler is the representative of the people
Because it separates religion from the state
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that in Islam all people are equal before the law and the ruler is the representative of the people. The lesson gives exactly this reason for calling Islam the most truly democratic system.

mcqs.q: The Quaid-e-Azam said that Pakistan should be built as a laboratory in order to:
options: Copy the British system of government
Enforce the practical system on Islamic principles
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to enforce the practical system on Islamic principles. The Quaid-e-Azam said Pakistan does not merely mean obtaining a piece of land; it should be a laboratory where a practical system based on Islamic principles can be enforced.

mcqs.q: At which event did the Quaid-e-Azam clarify the ideological basis of the Islamic state?
options: The Muslim League session at Lahore on 23 March 1940
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Muslim League session at Lahore on 23 March 1940. The lesson states that at this session the Quaid-e-Azam clarified the ideological basis of the Islamic state.

mcqs.q: What did the Quaid-e-Azam say about India in January 1941?
options: India is one country and one nation
India has never been one country or one nation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that India has never been one country or one nation. The lesson records this statement of the Quaid-e-Azam from January 1941, which supports the separate identity of the Muslims of the subcontinent.

mcqs.q: According to the Quaid-e-Azam, the two nations could not be merged into one nation because:
options: Hinduism and Islam are two separate social and civil systems
They lived in the same provinces
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that Hinduism and Islam are two separate social and civil systems. The Quaid-e-Azam gave this as the reason why the two nations could not be merged into one nation.

mcqs.q: Allama Iqbal gave his statement about the ideology of Pakistan in his presidential address at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allahabad, in December 1930. Allama Iqbal delivered his presidential address at the annual session of the All India Muslim League at Allahabad in December 1930 and presented the idea of a separate Muslim state.

mcqs.q: Which provinces did Allama Iqbal propose to combine into a separate state for the Muslims?
options: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan. In his Allahabad address Allama Iqbal said that these provinces should be combined into a separate state for the Muslims.

mcqs.q: According to Allama Iqbal, India is:
options: Not one country but a small subcontinent inhabited by people of different religions and languages
One country with one religion and one language
A single nation with a common culture
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that India is not one country but a small subcontinent inhabited by people of different religions and languages. This is how Allama Iqbal described India in his 1930 address, as the lesson records.

mcqs.q: The separate state proposed by Allama Iqbal would be the final destination of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Muslims of north-west India. The lesson states that the separate state formed from the combined north-western provinces would be the final destination of the Muslims of north-west India.

lessons.title: Revival and Reform Movements
lessons.notes_html:
Faraizi Movement

The Faraizi Movement was the movement of Haji Shariatullah (1760, Faridpur, Bengal). Its objectives were:

  • To revive Islamic customs among the Muslims of Bengal and end un-Islamic customs.
  • To guide Muslims to live according to Islamic teachings.
  • To protect the rights of the Muslim peasants of Bengal and to create self-confidence and self-respect in them.

Role of Shah Waliullah

Shah Waliullah (1703-1762, Delhi), seeing the religious and moral decline of the Muslims, began the work of reviving Islam.

  • He translated the Holy Quran into Persian so that common people could understand it.
  • In his famous book Hujjatullah al-Baligha: he presented Islam as a universal religion.
  • He invited Ahmad Shah Abdali, as a result of which the Marathas were defeated in the third Battle of Panipat in 1761.
  • His sons and grandsons also continued this work.

Struggle of Syed Ahmed Shaheed

Syed Ahmed Shaheed (1786, Rae Bareli) started the Mujahideen Movement: against polytheism, innovations and un-Islamic customs, to remove social evils from the Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

  • In 1826 he made Nowshera his centre.
  • He waged jihad against the Sikhs; Akora 1826 and the Hazro battles are part of this.
  • As Amir-ul-Momineen: he enforced Islamic laws in those areas.
  • Finally, on 6 May 1831, he was martyred fighting the Sikhs at Balakot, but his struggle became an example for the revival of Islamic society.

Aligarh Movement

Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817-1898) started the Aligarh Movement for the reawakening of the Muslims after the 1857 War of Independence.

  • By writing Asbab-e-Baghavat-e-Hind: he removed the doubts about Muslims from the minds of the British.
  • In 1862 he founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur and translated modern knowledge into Urdu.
  • He founded a school at Aligarh and then the M.A.O. College (1877).
  • Through the journal Tehzeeb-ul-Akhlaq: he attracted Muslims towards new education and science.
  • By supporting Urdu in the Urdu-Hindi controversy he laid the basis of the Two-Nation Theory.

Key Points

  • In the Aligarh Movement, the Scientific Society was founded in 1862 at Ghazipur.
  • Shah Waliullah died in the year 1762. Shah Waliullah died on 10 August 1762.

mcqs.q: Who started the Faraizi Movement?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Haji Shariatullah. The lesson states that the Faraizi Movement was the movement of Haji Shariatullah of Faridpur, Bengal, started to revive Islamic customs among the Muslims of Bengal.

mcqs.q: One objective of the Faraizi Movement was to:
options: Protect the rights of the Muslim peasants of Bengal
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to protect the rights of the Muslim peasants of Bengal. The lesson lists this among the objectives of the Faraizi Movement, along with reviving Islamic customs and creating self-confidence and self-respect among the Muslims.

mcqs.q: Shah Waliullah translated the Holy Quran into which language so that common people could understand it?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Persian. Seeing the religious and moral decline of the Muslims, Shah Waliullah translated the Holy Quran into Persian so that common people could understand it, as the lesson explains.

mcqs.q: The famous book of Shah Waliullah in which he presented Islam as a universal religion is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Hujjatullah al-Baligha. In this famous book Shah Waliullah presented Islam as a universal religion, as part of his work of reviving Islam among the Muslims of the subcontinent.

mcqs.q: On the invitation of Shah Waliullah, Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas in:
options: The third Battle of Panipat in 1761
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the third Battle of Panipat in 1761. Shah Waliullah invited Ahmad Shah Abdali, and as a result of his coming, the Marathas were defeated in the third Battle of Panipat in 1761.

mcqs.q: Syed Ahmed Shaheed made which place the centre of his Mujahideen Movement in 1826?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Nowshera. Syed Ahmed Shaheed started the Mujahideen Movement against polytheism, innovations and un-Islamic customs, and in 1826 he made Nowshera his centre for the struggle.

mcqs.q: Syed Ahmed Shaheed was martyred on 6 May 1831 while fighting the Sikhs at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Balakot. After his jihad against the Sikhs, in which the battles of Akora and Hazro also took place, Syed Ahmed Shaheed was martyred at Balakot on 6 May 1831, and his struggle became an example for the revival of Islamic society.

mcqs.q: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Scientific Society in 1862 at:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Ghazipur. In 1862 Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Scientific Society at Ghazipur and translated modern knowledge into Urdu for the benefit of the Muslims.

mcqs.q: The M.A.O. College at Aligarh was founded in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1877. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan first founded a school at Aligarh and then the M.A.O. College in 1877, as a major step of the Aligarh Movement for the reawakening of the Muslims.

mcqs.q: Through his journal Tehzeeb-ul-Akhlaq, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan attracted the Muslims towards:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is new education and science. The lesson states that through the journal Tehzeeb-ul-Akhlaq, Sir Syed Ahmed Khan attracted the Muslims towards new education and science after the 1857 War of Independence.

lessons.title: Two-Nation Theory and the Creation of Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
Two-Nation Theory

The Two-Nation Theory is that in India the Hindus and the Muslims are two separate nations: their religions, cultures, civilisations, laws, heroes and ways of life are quite different from each other, so they cannot live together as one nation.

  • Sir Syed Ahmed Khan was the first Muslim leader to use the word "nation" for the Muslims of the subcontinent.
  • Later Allama Iqbal (1930) and the Quaid-e-Azam carried this theory forward.

Role of the Muslim League

  • The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906 and protected the rights of the Muslims.
  • It concluded the Lucknow Pact in 1916.
  • It was reorganised by the Quaid-e-Azam in 1934.
  • It passed the Pakistan Resolution at Lahore on 23 March 1940.
  • It won the majority of Muslim seats in the 1945-46 elections.
  • It remained the central platform of the struggle for Pakistan up to the 3 June 1947 Plan.

Role of the Provinces

ProvinceRole
PunjabThe poetry of Allama Iqbal, the 1940 Lahore session, success in the 1945-46 elections, and the struggle of women and students
SindhThe 1938 Karachi session, support for the 1940 Resolution, and the Muslim League government in 1945-46
BalochistanThe spread of the Muslim League through the efforts of Qazi Muhammad Isa and the Shahi Jirga's decision to join Pakistan
Khyber PakhtunkhwaThe Muslim League's civil disobedience and the vote for Pakistan in the 1947 referendum

Creation of Pakistan

Under the 3 June 1947 Plan and the Indian Independence Act, the transfer of power was fixed in such a way that Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947 and India on 15 August 1947. According to the book, 14 August was the 27th of Ramadan (1366 AH), the night also called Shab-e-Qadr.

Responsibilities of the Citizens of an Ideological State

  • To live according to Islamic teachings and to establish a democratic system on Islamic principles.
  • Loyalty to the homeland and sacrifice when needed.
  • To earn a lawful livelihood and to get education.
  • To respect the law and to pay taxes.
  • To take part in constructive activities and in welfare work.
  • To uphold Muslim brotherhood and human dignity.

Character of the Quaid-e-Azam

The Quaid-e-Azam was a principled, honest, selfless, brave, steadfast, patient, wise and hard-working leader. He never compromised on his principles, never preferred personal interest over the interests of the Muslims, worked with a broad vision, and dedicated every moment of his life to Pakistan. These qualities of his character make him a model for all.

The Quaid-e-Azam as Governor General

  • He created national unity and said that now we are all only Pakistanis.
  • He rehabilitated 6.5 million refugees and set up the "Quaid-e-Azam Relief Fund".
  • He directed government officers to work with honesty and integrity.
  • He gave the message of ending provincial and racial discrimination.
  • On 1 July 1948 he inaugurated the State Bank and gave the guiding principles of Pakistan's economy.
  • He laid the foundations of foreign policy and advised students to pay full attention to education.
  • Despite illness he worked day and night until his last breath.

Key Points

  • The Muslim League was founded in 1906. The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906.
  • In Balochistan the Muslim League was founded by Qazi Muhammad Isa.
  • In 1936 Sindh became a separate province.
  • Pakistan came into being on the 27th of Ramadan.

mcqs.q: According to the Two-Nation Theory, the Hindus and the Muslims of India are:
options: One nation with a common culture
Two branches of the same nation
One nation divided by language only
Two separate nations with different religions, cultures, laws and ways of life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they are two separate nations. The Two-Nation Theory holds that the religions, cultures, civilisations, laws, heroes and ways of life of Hindus and Muslims are quite different, so they cannot live together as one nation.

mcqs.q: Who was the first Muslim leader to use the word 'nation' for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sir Syed Ahmed Khan. The lesson states that he was the first Muslim leader to use the word 'nation' for the Muslims of the subcontinent; later Allama Iqbal in 1930 and the Quaid-e-Azam carried this theory forward.

mcqs.q: The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 30 December 1906. The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on this date and from then on it protected the rights of the Muslims of the subcontinent.

mcqs.q: The Lucknow Pact was concluded by the Muslim League in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1916. After its foundation in 1906, the Muslim League concluded the Lucknow Pact in 1916, which the lesson lists among the League's important steps before the Pakistan Resolution.

mcqs.q: The Pakistan Resolution was passed by the Muslim League at Lahore on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 23 March 1940. On this date the Muslim League passed the Pakistan Resolution at Lahore, formally demanding a separate homeland for the Muslims of the subcontinent.

mcqs.q: In Balochistan, the Muslim League spread through the efforts of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Qazi Muhammad Isa. The lesson states that in Balochistan the Muslim League spread through his efforts, and the Shahi Jirga of Balochistan decided to join Pakistan.

mcqs.q: In Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the decision in favour of Pakistan in 1947 was made through:
options: A resolution of the Shahi Jirga
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a referendum. The lesson states that in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the Muslim League ran a civil disobedience movement and the people voted for Pakistan in the 1947 referendum.

mcqs.q: As Governor General, the Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1 July 1948. As Governor General, the Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank on this date and gave the guiding principles of Pakistan's economy.

mcqs.q: For the rehabilitation of the refugees, the Quaid-e-Azam set up:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Quaid-e-Azam Relief Fund. The lesson states that as Governor General he rehabilitated 6.5 million refugees and set up this fund for their relief.

mcqs.q: According to the book, 14 August 1947, the day Pakistan became independent, was:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the 27th of Ramadan, 1366 AH. The lesson notes that under the 3 June 1947 Plan Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947, which was the 27th of Ramadan, the night also called Shab-e-Qadr.

lessons.title: Importance of a Constitution, the Objectives Resolution and the 1956 Constitution
lessons.notes_html:
Need for a Constitution

A constitution is the body of laws and rules by which the system of a country or state and the business of government are run. Without a constitution no government can run in an organised way.

  • Through the constitution the organs of government are formed.
  • Through it their powers are fixed.
  • Through it the rights of citizens are protected.
  • Because of it every person remains bound by the law.

Objectives Resolution

The Objectives Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949. Its important features are:

  • All sovereignty and supreme authority over the universe belongs to Allah, and authority will be exercised by the people as a trust from Allah.
  • The principles of democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice presented by Islam will be enforced in the country.
  • Muslims will lead their individual and collective lives according to the principles of the Quran and Sunnah.
  • The rights of minorities will be protected.
  • Pakistan will be a federal state.
  • The fundamental rights and freedom of the people will be guaranteed.

Constitution of 1956

The Constitution of 1956 came into force on 23 March 1956. Its distinctive features are:

  • It stated at the outset that sovereignty and supreme authority belong to Allah and declared Pakistan an "Islamic Republic".
  • A federal parliamentary system of government was set up in the country.
  • The office of President replaced that of the Governor General.
  • Powers were divided between the centre and the provinces under the federal system.
  • Muslims were given every opportunity to live according to Islamic teachings.
  • The government would establish friendly relations with the Muslims of the world.
  • The head of state would be a Muslim.
  • No law could be made against the Quran and Sunnah.
  • The President would appoint a commission to recommend making the existing laws Islamic.
  • The rights of non-Muslim minorities were protected.

Key Points

  • Early man lived in the form of small tribes.
  • Immediately after its creation Pakistan needed a new constitution; until a new constitution was made, the Government of India Act 1935 was accepted as an interim constitution.
  • In the preamble of the Constitution of 1956 it is stated that sovereignty and supreme authority belongs to Allah.
  • Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly was dissolved by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad.

mcqs.q: What is a constitution?
options: The body of laws and rules by which the system of a country and the business of government are run
A speech of the head of state
A collection of court decisions only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the body of laws and rules by which the system of a country and the business of government are run. The lesson defines a constitution in these words and adds that without a constitution no government can run in an organised way.

mcqs.q: Until Pakistan's new constitution was made, which act was accepted as the interim constitution?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Government of India Act 1935. The lesson's key points state that immediately after its creation Pakistan needed a new constitution, and until one was made, the Government of India Act 1935 was accepted as the interim constitution.

mcqs.q: The Objectives Resolution was passed on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 12 March 1949. The Objectives Resolution was passed on this date and laid down the basic principles on which the future constitution of Pakistan was to be built.

mcqs.q: According to the Objectives Resolution, all sovereignty and supreme authority over the universe belongs to:
options: Allah, and authority is exercised by the people as a trust from Allah
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allah, with authority exercised by the people as a trust from Him. This is the first feature of the Objectives Resolution listed in the lesson, and it became the foundation of Pakistan's constitutional development.

mcqs.q: Under the Objectives Resolution, Pakistan was to be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a federal state. The Objectives Resolution declared that Pakistan will be a federal state, along with guaranteeing the fundamental rights and freedom of the people and protecting the rights of minorities.

mcqs.q: The Constitution of 1956 came into force on:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 23 March 1956. The first constitution of Pakistan came into force on this date and declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic with a federal parliamentary system of government.

mcqs.q: The Constitution of 1956 declared Pakistan as:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is an 'Islamic Republic'. The Constitution of 1956 stated at the outset that sovereignty and supreme authority belong to Allah and declared Pakistan an 'Islamic Republic'.

mcqs.q: Under the Constitution of 1956, the office of Governor General was replaced by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the office of President. The lesson lists this among the distinctive features of the 1956 Constitution, under which a federal parliamentary system was set up and powers were divided between the centre and the provinces.

mcqs.q: Under the Constitution of 1956, the head of state of Pakistan would be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a Muslim. The 1956 Constitution required the head of state to be a Muslim and also provided that no law could be made against the Quran and Sunnah.

mcqs.q: According to the Constitution of 1956, which of the following could NOT be done?
options: Powers could not be divided between the centre and the provinces
No law could be made against the Quran and Sunnah
The rights of minorities could not be protected
A federal system could not be set up
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that no law could be made against the Quran and Sunnah. This was a distinctive feature of the 1956 Constitution, while the federal system, the division of powers and the protection of minorities were all part of that constitution.

lessons.title: The 1973 Constitution and the Separation of East Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
Constitution of 1973

The Constitution of 1973 came into force on 14 August 1973. Its important points are:

  • The constitution was based on the Objectives Resolution.
  • The country's name was kept "Islamic Republic of Pakistan" and Islam was declared the state religion.
  • The definition of a Muslim was made part of the constitution.
  • The President and the Prime Minister will be Muslims.
  • The Objectives Resolution was included as the Preamble of the constitution.
  • A federal parliamentary system was set up in the country, with greater powers given to the Prime Minister.
  • Parliament consists of two houses: the Senate and the National Assembly.
  • Autonomy was given to the provinces.
  • Independence of the judiciary was declared necessary for the protection of the people's rights.
  • The Islamic Ideological Council was established.
  • Resolve was expressed to strengthen relations with Muslim countries.
  • Necessary steps will be taken for the promotion of Islamic teachings and the Arabic language.

Comparison of the Objectives Resolution and the Constitutions of 1956 and 1973

AspectObjectives Resolution (1949)Constitution of 1956Constitution of 1973
DatePassed on 12 March 1949Came into force on 23 March 1956Came into force on 14 August 1973
SovereigntySovereignty and supreme authority belongs to Allah; authority exercised by the people as a trustStated at the outset that sovereignty and supreme authority belong to AllahBased on the Objectives Resolution; the Resolution included as the Preamble
Status of the countryPakistan will be a federal statePakistan declared an "Islamic Republic"Name "Islamic Republic of Pakistan"; Islam the state religion
System of governmentPrinciples of democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice will be enforcedFederal parliamentary system; office of President replaced that of the Governor GeneralFederal parliamentary system; greater powers given to the Prime Minister; Parliament of two houses

Separation of East Pakistan

The causes of East Pakistan's separation given in the book are:

  • The geographical distance between the two wings, with India in between.
  • Differences in social and economic structure.
  • Repeated imposition of martial law and the language issue.
  • The demand for provincial autonomy and economic deprivation and propaganda about it.
  • The role of Hindu teachers and international conspiracies.
  • Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's majority in the 1970 elections and military action in East Pakistan.
  • India's attack.

As a result, on 16 December 1971 the Pakistani army laid down arms at Dhaka and East Pakistan became a separate country as "Bangladesh".

Role of Pakistanis for Prosperity

  • Work hard and progress in every field.
  • Rise above provincialism and regionalism.
  • Express love for Pakistan and patriotism through words and deeds.
  • Educate the young (new) generation.
  • Try to become self-reliant and avoid depending on loans or aid from others.
  • Help establish a system of government based on social justice and brotherhood.
  • Feel proud of being Pakistani.

Key Points

  • About forty heads of Muslim states took part in the Second Islamic Summit Conference.
  • Pakistan recognised Bangladesh during the Second Islamic Summit Conference (Lahore, February 1974).
  • The Constitution of 1973 is based on the Objectives Resolution.
  • In Pakistan's constitutions it is stated that supreme authority and supreme sovereignty belong to Allah.

mcqs.q: Under the Constitution of 1973, the Objectives Resolution was included as:

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Prime Minister. The lesson notes that the 1973 Constitution set up a federal parliamentary system in the country, with greater powers given to the Prime Minister.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is 16 December 1971. As a result of the causes listed in the lesson, the Pakistani army laid down arms at Dhaka on this date and East Pakistan became a separate country, Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: Pakistan recognised Bangladesh during:
options: The Second Islamic Summit Conference at Lahore in February 1974
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Second Islamic Summit Conference at Lahore in February 1974. The lesson's key points state that Pakistan recognised Bangladesh during this conference, in which about forty heads of Muslim states took part.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was a cause of the separation of East Pakistan, according to the book?

The geographical distance between the two wings, with India in between
The common language of both wings
The absence of any demand for provincial autonomy

mcqs.q: For Pakistan's prosperity, the lesson advises citizens to:
options: Depend on foreign loans and aid
Become self-reliant and avoid depending on loans or aid from others
Keep the young generation away from education

lessons.title: Location and Physical Features of Pakistan
lessons.notes_html:
Location of Pakistan

Pakistan is located in the south of South Asia and its location is of great importance.

  • China: In the north it is connected with China through the Karakoram Highway.
  • Afghanistan: It gives Afghanistan a route to reach the sea.
  • Iran and Central Asia: It is the basis of economic cooperation (E.C.O.) with Iran and Central Asia.
  • Arabian Sea: In the south is the Karachi port on the Arabian Sea, which is the gateway of trade with the Middle East and Europe.
  • Islamic world: It is one of the largest Islamic countries of the world and holds an important position in the Islamic world.

Physical Features of Pakistan

According to the book, the physical features of Pakistan can be divided into four parts:

  • Mountain ranges: The Himalayas, Karakoram and Hindu Kush in the north, Sulaiman and Kirthar in the west.
  • Plateaus: Pothohar and the Balochistan plateau.
  • Plains: The plains formed by the silt brought by the River Indus and its tributary rivers.
  • Desert and coastal areas: Thal, Cholistan, Thar, Kharan and a 1050 kilometre long coast.

Advantages of the Northern Mountain Ranges

  • They provide the country with natural defence and protection on one side.
  • They protect it from the cold winds coming from the North Pole.
  • In the monsoon season they cause rainfall and supply water to the rivers.
  • Their snow melts in summer and gives water for agriculture.
  • Most of the country's forests are in these very mountains, which are the country's wealth.

Neighbouring Countries and Borders

Key Points

  • The long border between Pakistan and Afghanistan is called the Durand Line. The common international border of Pakistan and Afghanistan is 2252 km long.
  • The coastal areas of Pakistan are Makran and Sindh. The Makran coast is between the Iranian border and the River Hub, and the other is the Sindh coast.
  • In the south-west of Pakistan our neighbouring country is Iran, with which Pakistan has a common border of about 800 km.
  • The area of Balochistan is 3,47,190 square kilometres. Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan.
  • The word FATA means Federally Administered Tribal Areas.
  • The largest salt mine of the world is in the province of Punjab (Khewra) in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Pakistan is connected with China in the north through:

mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. According to the book, the physical features of Pakistan can be divided into four parts: mountain ranges, plateaus, plains, and desert and coastal areas.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is the west. The lesson states that the Himalayas, Karakoram and Hindu Kush are in the north, while the Sulaiman and Kirthar ranges are in the west of the country.

mcqs.q: One advantage of the northern mountain ranges is that they:
options: Protect the country from the cold winds coming from the North Pole
Provide natural gas to the country
Join Pakistan with the Arabian Sea
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they protect the country from the cold winds coming from the North Pole. The lesson also lists their other advantages: natural defence, rainfall in the monsoon season, water for the rivers, and most of the country's forests.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1050 kilometres. The lesson mentions a 1050 kilometre long coast among the desert and coastal areas of Pakistan, lying along the Arabian Sea in the south.

mcqs.q: The common border between Pakistan and India is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1610 km. The lesson's table of neighbouring countries shows India in the east with a common border of 1610 km, while the common border with China in the north is 585 km.

mcqs.q: The long border between Pakistan and Afghanistan is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Durand Line. The lesson's key points state that the long border between Pakistan and Afghanistan is called the Durand Line and that this common international border is 2252 km long.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by area?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Balochistan. The lesson states that the area of Balochistan is 3,47,190 square kilometres and that Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: The largest salt mine in the world, Khewra, is located in the province of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Punjab. The lesson's key points state that the largest salt mine of the world is in the province of Punjab (Khewra) in Pakistan.

lessons.title: Climate and Environmental Pollution
lessons.notes_html:
What Is Meant by Climate?

The long-term weather condition of an area is called its climate, such as the average state of its temperature, rainfall (humidity) and wind. Weather is the condition of one day, while climate is the average of many years.

Climatic Regions of Pakistan

According to the book, Pakistan is divided into four climatic regions:

  • Mountainous climatic region: The northern and western mountain areas of Pakistan.
  • Plateau climatic region: Mostly the plateau area of Balochistan.
  • Plains climatic region: The upper plain of the River Indus (Punjab) and the lower plain (Sindh).
  • Coastal climatic region: The coastal areas of Sindh and Balochistan.

Effect of Climate on Human Life

Climate deeply affects human life: it determines people's ways of living, dress, food, occupations, games, customs and economic activities. In the cold northern areas people wear warm clothes, eat more meat and ghee, and stay confined to their homes in winter; while in the hot and plains areas people wear light clothes, eat rice and vegetables, and remain busy in agriculture and trade throughout the year.

Environmental Pollution

Environmental pollution means such undesirable changes in the land, water and air as are harmful to human and animal life. When various factors bring unhealthy changes upon our environment, it is called environmental pollution. It has three kinds: air pollution, water pollution and land pollution.

Population Increase and Pollution

With the increase in population, environmental pollution grows: more people need more vehicles, factories, houses and waste, which pollutes the air, water and land more. According to the book, in countries like Pakistan pollution is increasing day by day, and to reduce it, planting trees, disposing of waste properly and creating awareness among the people are necessary.

Key Points

  • Pakistan is divided into four climatic regions: mountainous, plateau, plains and coastal.
  • The climate of the upper plains of Pakistan is extreme (with severity of both heat and cold). In the plains areas there is severe heat in summer and severe cold in winter.
  • Air pollution is a major cause of the spoiling of water. The smoke and gases of factories and vehicles pollute the air and also spoil the water.
  • Water is about 70 percent of the weight of the human body.
  • The people of the northern areas of Pakistan remain busy in domestic (indoor) activities in winter, because of severe cold and snowfall they stay confined to their homes.
  • The River Hub and the Lyari flow in the Kirthar mountain range. To the south of the Kirthar range flow the River Hub and the Lyari stream, which finally fall into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

mcqs.q: What is meant by the climate of an area?
options: The weather of a single day
The rainfall of one season only
Its long-term weather condition, the average of many years
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the long-term weather condition, the average of many years. The lesson explains that climate is the average state of an area's temperature, rainfall and wind, while weather is the condition of one day.

mcqs.q: How does weather differ from climate?
options: Weather and climate are the same thing
Weather is the condition of one day, while climate is the average of many years
Weather covers many years, climate covers one day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that weather is the condition of one day, while climate is the average of many years. The lesson makes this clear distinction while defining what is meant by climate.

mcqs.q: Into how many climatic regions is Pakistan divided?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is four. According to the book, Pakistan is divided into four climatic regions: mountainous, plateau, plains and coastal.

mcqs.q: The plateau climatic region of Pakistan mostly covers:
options: The upper plain of the Indus
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the plateau area of Balochistan. The lesson lists the plateau climatic region as mostly the plateau area of Balochistan, separate from the mountainous, plains and coastal regions.

mcqs.q: Environmental pollution is divided into which three kinds?
options: Air pollution, noise pollution and light pollution
Water pollution, soil pollution and heat pollution
Air pollution, water pollution and land pollution
Land pollution, noise pollution and air pollution
mcqs.why: The correct answer is air pollution, water pollution and land pollution. The lesson states that environmental pollution — undesirable changes in the land, water and air that are harmful to life — has these three kinds.

mcqs.q: With the increase in population, environmental pollution grows because:
options: More people need more vehicles, factories and houses and produce more waste
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that more people need more vehicles, factories and houses and produce more waste. The lesson explains that with the increase in population, pollution of the air, water and land grows, and it can be reduced by planting trees and disposing of waste properly.

mcqs.q: According to the book, a major cause of the spoiling of water is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is air pollution. The lesson's key points state that air pollution is a major cause of the spoiling of water, because the smoke and gases of factories and vehicles pollute the air and also spoil the water.

mcqs.q: About what percentage of the weight of the human body is water?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is about 70 percent. This fact is given in the lesson's key points while discussing water and its importance for human life.

mcqs.q: In the cold northern areas of Pakistan, people in winter:
options: Wear light clothes and eat rice and vegetables
Wear warm clothes, eat more meat and ghee, and stay confined to their homes
Remain busy in trade throughout the year
Work in the fields day and night
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they wear warm clothes, eat more meat and ghee, and stay confined to their homes. The lesson explains that climate affects dress, food and occupations, and in the northern areas people stay indoors in winter because of severe cold and snowfall.

mcqs.q: The River Hub and the Lyari, which flow in the Kirthar range, finally fall into:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Arabian Sea near Karachi. The lesson's key points state that to the south of the Kirthar range flow the River Hub and the Lyari stream, which finally fall into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

lessons.title: Types and Importance of Resources and Moderation
lessons.notes_html:
Importance of Resources

Resources are the real wealth and capital of a nation. They bring progress and prosperity to the country, help in the protection and defence of the country, fulfil the material needs of the citizens, promote trade and industry, provide employment to the people, and strengthen national unity. Where human and natural resources are abundant and properly used, that country progresses.

Types of Resources

According to the book, resources are of two kinds:

  • Human resources (Man Power): people's ability, capacity, skill and labour.
  • Natural resources: things granted by Allah, such as land and soil, forests, minerals, water, energy resources, agriculture and livestock.

How Human Resources and Other Resources Depend on Each Other

Human resources and other resources depend on each other. Natural resources — land, forests, minerals and water — lie useless in their place until man benefits from them through his labour, knowledge and skill, and man needs other resources — food, clothes, housing and energy — to live. Therefore, for the progress of the country, the joint use of both kinds of resources is necessary.

Moderation in Life

Moderation in life means that a person lives within his available resources — he stretches his feet according to his blanket. Moderation, the middle path, is a reasonable and balanced attitude in every matter of life: economic, social and political. It brings peace and prosperity to society, while extremism causes evils. Islam teaches moderation in every sphere of life.

Key Points

  • The people who are busy in different works are called human resources. The ability, capacity and skill of the people who are busy in different professions and employments are called human resources.
  • Moderation in life means the middle path — living within one's available resources and adopting a balanced attitude in every matter.

mcqs.q: Resources are described in the lesson as:
options: The real wealth and capital of a nation
Only the money in the banks
Only the buildings of the government
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the real wealth and capital of a nation. The lesson states that resources bring progress and prosperity to the country, fulfil the material needs of the citizens, promote trade and industry and provide employment.

mcqs.q: How many kinds of resources are there, according to the book?
options: Two — human resources and natural resources
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two — human resources and natural resources. Human resources are people's ability, capacity, skill and labour, while natural resources are the things granted by Allah, such as land, forests, minerals and water.

mcqs.q: Human resources (man power) mean:
options: The ability, capacity, skill and labour of the people
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the ability, capacity, skill and labour of the people. The lesson defines human resources as the ability, capacity and skill of the people who are busy in different professions and employments.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a natural resource?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is minerals. Natural resources are the things granted by Allah, such as land and soil, forests, minerals, water, energy resources, agriculture and livestock, while skill, labour and ability are human resources.

mcqs.q: Why do natural resources remain useless without human resources?
options: Because they are found only in mountains
Because the government does not allow their use
Because they belong to other countries
Because they lie in their place until man benefits from them through his labour, knowledge and skill
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they lie in their place until man benefits from them through his labour, knowledge and skill. The lesson says the two kinds of resources depend on each other, and their joint use is necessary for the progress of the country.

mcqs.q: What does moderation in life mean?
options: Giving up all needs of life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is living within one's available resources. The lesson explains moderation with the saying that a person stretches his feet according to his blanket, that is, he lives within his available resources.

mcqs.q: Moderation is described in the lesson as:
options: The middle path — a reasonable and balanced attitude in every matter of life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the middle path — a reasonable and balanced attitude in every matter of life. The lesson adds that moderation brings peace and prosperity to society, while extremism causes evils, and Islam teaches moderation in every sphere of life.

mcqs.q: According to the lesson, what does extremism in life cause?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is evils in society. The lesson contrasts moderation, which brings peace and prosperity to society, with extremism, which causes evils.

mcqs.q: One importance of resources for a country is that they:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they provide employment to the people. The lesson lists the importance of resources: they bring prosperity, help in the protection and defence of the country, fulfil material needs, promote trade and industry, provide employment and strengthen national unity.

mcqs.q: For the progress of a country, what is necessary regarding the two kinds of resources?
options: The joint use of both human and natural resources
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the joint use of both human and natural resources. The lesson concludes that because human resources and other resources depend on each other, their joint use is necessary for the progress of the country.

lessons.title: Natural Resources of Pakistan — Forests, Minerals, Agriculture and Energy
lessons.notes_html:
Advantages of Forests

Fourteen advantages of forests are given in the book, the important ones being:

  • Forests are among the important resources of the country and provide timber, building wood and fuel.
  • They help maintain the fertility of the land and stop soil erosion.
  • They keep the temperature moderate and cause rainfall.
  • They are the home of wildlife.
  • They add to the beauty of the land and become centres of tourism.
  • They clean the air and provide oxygen.

Agricultural Resources of Pakistan

The agricultural resources of Pakistan are the things with which agriculture is done: fertile land and different kinds of soil, water for irrigation — rivers, canals and tube wells — seed, fertiliser, agricultural machinery, hard-working farmers and a favourable climate. Pakistan is basically an agricultural country; about 55 percent of the people are connected with agriculture and a large share of the national income comes from agriculture.

The agricultural resources of Pakistan, in the form of crops, are:

  • Cash crops: cotton, sugarcane, tobacco and oilseeds.
  • Food crops: wheat, rice, maize, sorghum, millet, pulses and barley.
  • Vegetables and fruits: potato, onion, tomato, mango, banana, orange, apple, grapes and dry fruits.

Atomic (Nuclear) Energy

Atomic energy is obtained from elements like uranium. In Pakistan atomic energy is used for peaceful purposes.

  • The Karachi Nuclear Power Plant, which started work in 1971, and the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant, which in 2002 generated 300 MW, generate electricity.
  • Institutions like NIFA work for agricultural research.
  • Nuclear treatment centres are working for the treatment of cancer at Karachi, Jamshoro, Lahore, Multan, Bahawalpur, Islamabad, Peshawar, Quetta and Faisalabad.

Key Points

  • The soil formed from the flood layers of soil and silt is called the plains soil of the River Indus (river-borne soil). This soil was formed by the collection of the soil and silt flowing along with the River Indus.
  • Mountain forests are found in the northern and western mountain areas, such as Swat, Dir, Chitral, Abbottabad and Murree.
  • The place in Pakistan where natural gas was found for the first time is called Sui. Natural gas was first found in 1952 at Sui in Balochistan.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they help maintain the fertility of the land and stop soil erosion. The lesson lists fourteen advantages of forests, including providing timber and fuel, keeping the temperature moderate, causing rainfall, cleaning the air and being the home of wildlife.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is cotton. The lesson lists the cash crops of Pakistan as cotton, sugarcane, tobacco and oilseeds, while wheat, rice and maize are food crops.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is about 55 percent. The lesson states that Pakistan is basically an agricultural country, about 55 percent of its people are connected with agriculture and a large share of the national income comes from agriculture.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is Sui in Balochistan. The lesson's key points state that the place in Pakistan where natural gas was found for the first time is Sui, and that natural gas was first found there in 1952.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1971. The lesson states that atomic energy is used for peaceful purposes in Pakistan and that the Karachi Nuclear Power Plant started work in 1971 to generate electricity.

mcqs.q: The Chashma Nuclear Power Plant generated how much electricity in 2002?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 300 MW. The lesson states that the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant generated 300 MW of electricity in 2002, showing the peaceful use of atomic energy in Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Atomic energy is obtained from elements like:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is uranium. The lesson explains that atomic energy is obtained from elements like uranium and that in Pakistan it is used for peaceful purposes, such as generating electricity and the treatment of cancer.

options: Swat, Dir, Chitral, Abbottabad and Murree
Multan, Bahawalpur and Rahim Yar Khan

lessons.title: Industry and National Development
lessons.notes_html:
What is Meant by Industry?

The work or establishment of producing goods in factories through machines is called industry. In the broad sense, industry means making such goods as fulfil people's needs and bring benefit. In the early period industry was simple and based on hand work; now modern industry is based on machines and large-scale production.

National Progress

Progress in the economic and social sectors is called national progress. Discovering resources and using them for the maximum benefit of the people is called national progress. National progress reflects the strength and stability of human and natural resources, through which life becomes easy and better.

Importance of Industry in National Progress

For the progress of any country, after agriculture and the discovery of natural resources, industry is an essential thing. Through industry:

  • The country's economic progress takes place.
  • The price of goods made from raw material increases.
  • People get employment.
  • People get comforts.
  • The country's economy becomes strong and political stability is helped.
  • The country becomes self-sufficient and the standard of living rises.

Steps for the Promotion of Industrial Progress

According to the book, these steps should be taken for the promotion of industrial progress in Pakistan:

  • The law-and-order situation in the country should be improved so that investors invest without any fear.
  • The rules and regulations for trade should be made easy.
  • During practical training, a sense of the dignity of labour should be created.
  • A strict system of quality control should be established.
  • The standard of education in marketing and business administration should be improved.
  • Industrial policies should be completely clear, transparent and plain.
  • The government should give concessions in taxes to industrialists.
  • The conditions of workers should be improved and their wages increased.

Key Points

  • For economic progress, investment in industry is necessary.
  • The negative attitude of labour associations (trade unions) is a problem for our industry.

mcqs.q: What is meant by industry?
options: Producing goods by hand at home
The work of producing goods in factories through machines
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the work of producing goods in factories through machines. The lesson explains that in the early period industry was simple and based on hand work, while modern industry is based on machines and large-scale production.

mcqs.q: National progress means:
options: Progress in the economic and social sectors
mcqs.why: The correct answer is progress in the economic and social sectors. The lesson defines national progress in these words and says it also means discovering resources and using them for the maximum benefit of the people.

mcqs.q: National progress reflects:
options: The size of the population only
The strength and stability of human and natural resources
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the strength and stability of human and natural resources. The lesson states that national progress reflects this strength and stability, through which life becomes easy and better.

mcqs.q: Through industry, the price of goods made from raw material:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is increases. The lesson lists this among the importance of industry in national progress: goods made from raw material get a higher price, people get employment and the country's economy becomes strong.

mcqs.q: One benefit of industry is that the country:
options: Becomes self-sufficient and the standard of living rises
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the country becomes self-sufficient and the standard of living rises. The lesson includes this among the benefits of industry, along with economic progress, employment and comforts for the people.

mcqs.q: The law-and-order situation in the country should be improved so that:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is so that investors invest without any fear. This is the first step the book recommends for the promotion of industrial progress in Pakistan, followed by making the rules and regulations for trade easy.

mcqs.q: Which step is recommended in the book for the promotion of industrial progress?
options: A strict system of quality control should be established
Industrial policies should be kept secret
Taxes on industrialists should be raised sharply
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a strict system of quality control should be established. The book's steps for industrial promotion include this, along with easy trade rules, clear and transparent industrial policies and tax concessions for industrialists.

mcqs.q: The government should give which facility to industrialists for the promotion of industry?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is concessions in taxes. The lesson lists this among the steps for the promotion of industrial progress, together with improving the conditions of workers and increasing their wages.

mcqs.q: According to the book, for economic progress it is necessary to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to invest in industry. The lesson's key points state plainly that for economic progress, investment in industry is necessary.

mcqs.q: According to the key points, what is a problem for our industry?
options: The negative attitude of labour associations (trade unions)
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the negative attitude of labour associations (trade unions). The lesson's key points name this as a problem for our industry, which is why the book also recommends improving the conditions of workers and increasing their wages.

lessons.title: Major Industries, Means of Transport and E-Commerce
lessons.notes_html:
Cotton Textile Industry

The cotton textile industry is the backbone of Pakistan's economy. Pakistan has become self-sufficient in the cotton textile industry and earns billions of rupees of foreign exchange every year. At the time of independence there were only three cotton textile mills in the country; now about 500 mills are working. The important centres are Faisalabad, Lahore, Multan, Karachi and Hyderabad.

Sugar Industry

The sugar industry is one of the large industries of the country. In 1947 Pakistan had only one sugar mill; now there are 78 sugar mills in the country — 40 in Punjab, 32 in Sindh and 6 in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — with a production capacity of 5 million tons. Pakistan is self-sufficient in sugar production.

Means of Transport and National Progress

The means of transport help national progress in this way:

  • They promote the country's agriculture and industry.
  • They promote national and international trade.
  • They join the people of the different regions of the country with one another and strengthen national unity.
  • They strengthen the country's defence.
  • In case of natural calamities, such as flood and earthquake, they quickly deliver relief.
  • They carry raw material to factories and finished goods to markets.

The National Highway

The National Highway (N-5) is the oldest and most important highway of Pakistan, with a length of 1735 km. It starts from Karachi and goes to Peshawar. The famous cities located on it are Hyderabad, Sukkur, Bahawalpur, Multan, Lahore, Gujranwala, Rawalpindi and Peshawar. The portion of this highway between Lahore and Peshawar is called the G.T. Road (Grand Trunk Road).

E-Commerce

E-commerce means doing trade through computer and internet.

  • Trade transactions take place very quickly.
  • A trader can contact traders in any part of the world and tell them the details, prices and quantities of his goods.
  • A buyer can buy things sitting at home.
  • The foundations of e-commerce are getting strong in Pakistan and the facility of home delivery exists in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad, Peshawar and other cities.

Key Points

  • Pakistan is self-sufficient in the production of sugar and is also earning valuable foreign exchange from the export of sugar.
  • Sialkot is famous for sports goods. Pakistani sports goods, such as cricket bats, hockey and football, are famous all over the world.

lessons.notes_html:
Composition of Population

According to the 1998 census, the total population of Pakistan was 132,352,279 and the density of population was 166 persons per square kilometre. 67.5% of the population lives in villages and 32.5% in cities.

Language-wise, the composition is: Punjabi 44.15%, Pashto 15.42%, Sindhi 14.12%, Saraiki 10.53%, Urdu 7.57%, Balochi 3.55% and others 4.66%.

State of Literacy

The state of literacy in Pakistan is not encouraging. In 1951 the literacy rate was 13.2%, which rose to 45% in 1998 — men 61% and women 36%. Literacy is a great blessing, and it is a danger bell for the country's progress that still more than half the people are illiterate. The government is setting up new institutions to increase literacy and is running programmes like “Education for All”.

Effects of Population Growth and Migration

Population growth and migration from villages to cities affect national progress in this way:

  • Pressure on resources increases and per-person resources decrease.
  • Shortage of housing, water, electricity, transport and employment arises in cities.
  • Unemployment increases.
  • Health and education facilities become insufficient.
  • On the other hand, if the population is given education and skills, it can become a human resource and help progress.

lessons.title: Population Growth — Causes, Effects and Balance
lessons.notes_html:
Causes of Population Growth

According to the book, the causes of population growth in Pakistan are:

  • Social factor: Pakistan is an Islamic country; many people believe that children are a blessing given by Allah and a large family is considered strength.
  • Refusal of family planning: some religious leaders consider family planning a sin.
  • Lack of education: especially the literacy rate among women is low.
  • Early marriage: early marriage causes an increase in the birth of children.
  • Poverty: the birth rate is higher in poor families.
  • Desire for a son: the desire for the birth of a son also causes more children to be born.

Balance Between Population and Resources

Balance between the growing population and the strength of resources can be maintained in this way:

  • The growth rate of the population should be reduced.
  • The production of resources should be increased through progress in agriculture, industry and trade.
  • Education and training should be spread so that people become productive.
  • New resources should be found, such as new reserves of minerals and oil.
  • Uninhabited land should be settled and barren land brought under cultivation.

Effects on Health

With population growth, health facilities become insufficient: doctors, hospitals and medicines fall short, the death rate of mothers and children rises, and malnutrition increases. In Pakistan the death rate of children under five years is 102 per thousand.

Effects on Education

With population growth, schools, teachers and books fall short, the number of children in classes increases, the literacy rate stays low and the standard of education falls.

Key Points

  • The most important problem of Pakistan is population growth, which causes pressure on resources, unemployment and shortage of health and education facilities.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that early marriage increases the birth of children. The book lists early marriage among the causes of population growth, along with lack of education, poverty and the desire for a son.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that doctors, hospitals and medicines fall short of the needs. The lesson says that with population growth, health facilities become insufficient and the death rate of mothers and children rises.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is that schools, teachers and books fall short and the number of children in classes increases. As a result, the lesson says, the literacy rate stays low and the standard of education falls.

lessons.title: Culture, Languages and the National Language Urdu
lessons.notes_html:
Characteristics of Culture

According to the book, the characteristics of culture are:

  • Every culture has its own particular temperament, which distinguishes it from other cultures.
  • Culture is a force (a motive) which influences others.
  • Culture can change through meeting and contact with other cultures.
  • The identity and recognition of any culture lie in its own individuality.
  • Every culture holds certain values and absorbs them within itself.

Importance of Language in Culture

Language is the most important part of culture, because language is the most effective means of expressing thoughts, feelings and emotions. A nation is recognised through its language, and every nation holds its language dear. The national language joins the people living in different regions with one another and creates national unity and solidarity.

Languages of Pakistan

More than 30 languages are spoken in Pakistan. The major provincial languages are Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Pashto, Balochi and Saraiki.

LanguageRegion and Details
UrduThe national language; in the Constitution of 1973 it was declared the official language
SindhiSindh; one of the oldest languages of South Asia and the official language of Sindh
PunjabiPunjab; great Sufi poets: Baba Farid, Shah Hussain, Sultan Bahu and Bulleh Shah
PashtoKhyber Pakhtunkhwa; famous poets: Rahman Baba and Khushhal Khan Khattak
BalochiBalochistan; famous writers: Jam Durrak and Mast Tawakli
OthersSaraiki, Hindko, Brahui, Kashmiri, Shina and other languages

Importance of Urdu as the National Language

  • Urdu is the national language of Pakistan and the means of communication; it is spoken and understood in all four provinces.
  • It is a means of national unity and solidarity and joins the people of the different provinces with one another.
  • At the time of the creation of Pakistan, the founder of Pakistan, Quaid-e-Azam, announced in clear words that the national language of Pakistan would be Urdu.
  • Urdu is a language with a large treasure of learning and literature, with poetry, prose, drama and films.
  • Urdu has enriched itself by taking words from the languages of all the regions of Pakistan.

Key Points

  • The national language of Pakistan is Urdu.
  • The culture of Pakistan is a common (shared) culture, in which the good qualities of all the regions and languages are included.
  • More than 30 languages are spoken in Pakistan.
  • In Balochistan two languages, Balochi and Brahui, are spoken; Pashto is also spoken.
  • The two great poets of the Balochi language are Jam Durrak and Mast Tawakli.
  • Shah Hussain is a great Punjabi Sufi poet.
  • After independence the Sindhi language made immense progress in prose and poetry.

lessons.title: Common Cultural Features, Arts and Festivals
lessons.notes_html:
Common Cultural Manifestations in National Life

  • National language: the common national language Urdu.
  • Beliefs and values: Islamic beliefs and values.
  • Social life: simplicity, belief in old traditions, the joint family system and respect for elders.
  • Food: the simple diet of most people — wheat bread, meat, pulses and vegetables — and hospitality.
  • Recreation: cricket, hockey, squash, kabaddi and wrestling.
  • Religious festivals: Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Azha and Eid Milad-un-Nabi.
  • Sufi message: the one message of brotherhood and love given by the Sufis in different languages.
  • Communication and education: the means of communication — radio, TV and newspapers — and the education system.

Arts and Artists of Pakistan

There are several fields of art and literature in Pakistan. Painting, calligraphy, architecture and music are important arts; these arts spread widely in South Asia during the Muslim period of rule.

  • Handicrafts: Sindhi ajrak, fragrant shawls, Kashmiri shawls, Balochi embroidery and Punjab's clay pots are famous.
  • Fairs and festivals: Eids, Milad, urs and fairs.
  • Literature: the great poets and writers of Urdu, Sindhi, Punjabi, Pashto and Balochi literature, such as Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai, Baba Farid, Rahman Baba and Jam Durrak.

These arts are the beauty and identity of Pakistan's culture.

Importance of Festivals

  • Festivals bring joy and happiness to the people.
  • People meet one another, give gifts and share in one another's grief and joy.
  • Religious festivals — Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Azha and Eid Milad-un-Nabi — strengthen the faith and unity of Muslims.
  • Non-Muslim Pakistanis also celebrate their festivals — Christmas, Diwali, Holi and Baisakhi — and Muslims share in their joys.
  • Fairs and urs, such as the Urs of Data Ganj Bakhsh and the Urs of Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai, are signs of our common cultural heritage.

Key Points

  • The national dress of Pakistan is shalwar and qameez. Men generally wear shalwar qameez and the common dress of women is also shalwar qameez and dupatta.
  • Most of the people of Pakistan eat simple food — wheat bread, meat, pulses and vegetables.
  • The one message of brotherhood and love is what our Sufis gave in different languages.
  • Eid-ul-Fitr is celebrated in the month of Shawwal, on 1 Shawwal.
  • Christians celebrate Christmas on 25 December.

lessons.title: Importance of Education and the National Education Policy
lessons.notes_html:
Importance of Education

Without education real progress is not possible. Through education people are helped to use their natural abilities, the outlook and thinking of the nation change, and national unity and the spirit of patriotism grow.

  • Citizens become aware of their rights and duties.
  • People's creative abilities are promoted.
  • Economic progress takes place and the standard of living rises.
  • The protection and use of natural resources become possible.
  • For the development of human resources, education is the best investment.

National Education Policy 1998 to 2010

The important aspects of this policy are that every citizen has the right to get the facility of education, and all resources will be used to end illiteracy.

  • By 2010 the enrolment rate of children of the early age group, 5-9 years, will be raised to 100%.
  • The law of compulsory primary education will be passed and enforced by 2004-05.
  • Technical education will be promoted and a programme of teachers' training will be started.
  • The national budget for education will be raised from 2.2% to 4%.
  • Religious seminaries will be included in the education system.

Social and Cultural Importance of Education

Political aspect: Education is the first condition for the success of democracy. Educated people express their opinion and hold their political leaders accountable.

Social and cultural aspect: Through education social customs and cultural values become strong, and people become aware of their civilisation and culture.

Economic aspect: Through education people's income and standard of living increase, and educated people play a better role in industry, trade and services.

Key Points

  • Without education real progress is not possible.
  • The first educational conference in Pakistan was held in 1947.
  • A law of compulsory primary education came into force.

lessons.title: Education Structure, Teacher Training, Technical Education and Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Structure of Formal Education

Formal education in Pakistan begins from primary, that is, from class one. The levels of its structure are as follows:

LevelClassesDuration
PrimaryFrom class 1 to class 55 years
MiddleFrom class 6 to class 83 years
SecondaryClasses 9 and 102 years
Higher SecondaryClasses 11 and 122 years
DegreeB.A., B.Sc. etc.2 years
UniversityUp to M.A., M.Sc., M.Phil. and Ph.D.-

Components of the Secondary Curriculum

  • Compulsory subjects: Urdu, English, Islamiat, Pakistan Studies.
  • Science group: Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics.
  • Commerce group: Commerce group subjects.
  • Arts group: History, Geography, Economics and Civics.
  • Optional subjects: At the secondary level students have to choose one group from science, commerce or arts.

Teacher Training

  • P.T.C.: One year of training for primary teachers.
  • C.T.: One year of training for middle teachers.
  • B.Ed. and M.Ed.: B.Ed. is one year of training and M.Ed. is one more year of training for secondary teachers.
  • Allama Iqbal Open University gives teacher training through its distance system. In the National Education Policy 1998 to 2010 the courses of teacher training have been modernised, but there are still several problems, such as inexperienced teachers and lack of financial resources for training.

Technical and Professional Education

In the modern age, technical experts are needed for industrial progress. The government has opened polytechnic institutions and technical training centres in the country, such as the Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute at Topi (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa). Through technical education a student can gain skill in one profession and get employment. Professional education includes medicine, engineering, commerce, agriculture and law. Through technical and professional education the country's economy becomes strong and unemployment decreases.

Problems in the Field of Education

  • The role of landlords is the biggest obstacle in the way of poor children's education.
  • Dropout: About 85% of children get admitted to primary schools but only 56% complete the fifth year.
  • Absence of teachers, heavy fees of private educational institutions, and lack of equipment and facilities in schools — many schools do not even have a boundary wall, clean water and furniture.
  • Non-availability of textbooks, lack of hostel accommodation for students, and political interference.

Objectives of I.T. in Education

  • To modernise Pakistan's education system at every level through the use of I.T.
  • To get access to research and modern data through the internet.
  • To popularise I.T. among children of every age and prepare them for the coming decade.
  • To use the computer in different roles to make teaching effective in the classroom.
  • To use means of communication (e-mail etc.) for teachers' training and other educational activities.

Key Points

  • Formal education in Pakistan begins from primary (class one).
  • Professional education includes education in engineering, medicine, commerce and agriculture.
